title: Origins and History
description: Origins and History. American football grew out of rugby and soccer played at American colleges in the late 1800s, with the first college game played in 1869 between Rutgers and Princeton Walter Camp, called the father of American football, shaped the game with the line of scrimmage, the system of downs, and eleven players a side Early teams ran the ball almost exclusively, and the forward pass, legalized in 1906, opened the modern passing game In practice, Study old formations first, then trace how each rule change opened a new kind of play.

demo.code:
# American Football: Origins and History - avg calculator
A = 1869
B = 1920
print('Values: %s and %s' % (A, B))
print('Average: %.2f' % ((A + B) / 2.0))
print('Total: %s' % (A + B))

history: American football grew out of rugby and soccer played at American colleges in the late 1800s, with the first college game played in 1869 between Rutgers and Princeton
rules: Walter Camp, called the father of American football, shaped the game with the line of scrimmage, the system of downs, and eleven players a side
techniques: Early teams ran the ball almost exclusively, and the forward pass, legalized in 1906, opened the modern passing game

title: Rules and the Field
description: Rules and the Field. The field is 100 yards long between goal lines, with a 10-yard end zone at each end, and yard lines marked every five yards A team has four downs to advance ten yards or it turns the ball over, and a game lasts four quarters of fifteen minutes in the professional game Down, distance, and field position decide whether a team runs, passes, punts, or kicks In practice, Walk a field with a rulebook, calling the down and distance aloud on every imaginary snap.

demo.code:

A = 100
B = 10
print('Made: %s of %s attempts' % (A, B))
print('Success rate: %.1f%%' % (100.0 * A / B))
print('Missed: %s' % (B - A))
demo.expected_output:
Made: 100 of 10 attempts
Success rate: 1000.0%
Missed: -90

rules: A team has four downs to advance ten yards or it turns the ball over, and a game lasts four quarters of fifteen minutes in the professional game
techniques: Down, distance, and field position decide whether a team runs, passes, punts, or kicks

title: Offense Positions
description: Offense Positions. The offense grew from a single ball carrier behind blockers into eleven specialized roles built around the quarterback The quarterback takes the snap and passes, hands off, or runs, protected by five linemen and supported by receivers, backs, and tight ends Receivers run timed routes against coverages, backs read blocks, and linemen use footwork and leverage to hold the line In practice, Drill one position at a time, then combine routes and blocking in seven-on-seven work.

demo.code:

A = 11
B = 5
print('Sessions per week: %s, weeks: %s' % (A, B))
print('Total sessions: %s' % (A * B))
print('Sessions in half the block: %s' % (A * B // 2))
demo.expected_output:
Sessions per week: 11, weeks: 5
Total sessions: 55
Sessions in half the block: 27

techniques: Receivers run timed routes against coverages, backs read blocks, and linemen use footwork and leverage to hold the line

title: Defense Positions
description: Defense Positions. Defenses answered the passing game with specialized cover men and pass rushers, moving from simple seven-man fronts to modern nickel and dime packages Defensive linemen attack the backfield, linebackers stop runs and cover short passes, and defensive backs defend receivers deep Tackling with the head up and the shoulder leading, shedding blocks, and reading the quarterback's eyes are core defensive skills In practice, Practice tackling form without contact first, then add pursuit angles and coverage drops.

print('Midpoint year: %s' % ((A + B) // 2))
demo.expected_output:
Earlier year: 7, later year: 4
Span: -3 years
Midpoint year: 5

rules: Defensive linemen attack the backfield, linebackers stop runs and cover short passes, and defensive backs defend receivers deep
techniques: Tackling with the head up and the shoulder leading, shedding blocks, and reading the quarterback's eyes are core defensive skills

Kicking has been part of football since its rugby roots, and the punt, kickoff, and placekick each became a specialist's job Kickoffs start halves and follow scores, punts trade possession for field position, and a field goal scores three points while a conversion after a touchdown scores one or two Punters aim for hang time and placement, kickers rehearse a repeatable approach, and coverage teams sprint in lanes to the returner In practice, Rehearse the snap, hold, and kick as one timed unit before adding rushers.

title: The Passing Game
description: The Passing Game. The forward pass was legalized in 1906 and grew from a rare trick into the center of most modern offenses A pass must be thrown from behind the line of scrimmage, a receiver must catch it in bounds, and an incomplete pass stops the clock Quarterbacks read coverages before and after the snap, throw receivers open, and use timing routes that break as the ball arrives In practice, Throw routes on air daily, then add defenders and read one coverage at a time.

print('Converted (x 0.9144): %.2f' % (A * 0.9144))
print('Converted back: %.2f' % (A * 0.9144 / 0.9144))

title: The Running Game
description: The Running Game. Running was the whole game in its first decades, and power running, sweeps, and option plays still anchor many offenses The ball carrier follows blockers through a designed gap, and a run ends when the carrier is downed, pushed out, or scores Zone blocking lets backs cut to daylight, power blocking seals a gap, and play-action fakes a run to free a pass In practice, Run footwork ladders and sled drives, then practice reading the first blocker's movement.

Ratio A:B = 2.500
Share of A: 71.4%

techniques: Zone blocking lets backs cut to daylight, power blocking seals a gap, and play-action fakes a run to free a pass
